chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ja'far ibn Yahya al-Khaza'i, from one of our companions, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'I bought a slave girl who was not of legitimate birth (born out of wedlock), and she was with me in every opportunity.' He said, 'Ask about her mother, to whom she belonged, so ask him to make permissible what he had done with her mother, in order for the child to be legitimate.'

key_terms.غَيْرِ رِشْدَةٍ: Not of legitimate birth / Born out of wedlock
key_terms.لِيَطِيبَ الْوَلَدُ: In order for the child to be legitimate/clear

ai.seo_question: How to legitimize the children of a slave girl born out of wedlock in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines the specific mechanism of 'Istibra'' (verification of lineage) for a slave girl of uncertain parentage, emphasizing the need to trace her biological father to establish clear lineage. In Shia jurisprudence, this process ensures the child's legitimacy and inheritance rights by linking them to a known patriarch, often through the father acknowledging paternity or marrying the mother. It highlights the importance of social and legal clarity in family structures within the early Islamic community.
